question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping maintains firm control over the Chinese Communist Party through abolished presidential term limits, loyal appointments across the Politburo and Central Military Commission, and sustained anti-corruption purges that have targeted senior military and civilian figures as recently as early 2026. Recent elite gatherings, including the August Beidaihe conclave, have focused on preparations for the 2027 party congress without signaling any leadership transition, while Xi's public schedule and policy directives show no disruption from health or factional challenges. This centralized authority and absence of verifiable succession signals underpin the near-certain trader consensus against removal before 2027. Sudden medical events, internal elite fractures, or major external crises remain low-probability factors that could still shift outcomes within the opaque system.

eventMetadata.context_description: The 2028 Democratic presidential nomination market remains tightly contested because a fragmented field of governors, senators, and House progressives lacks a dominant consensus candidate following the party's 2024 defeat. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez has gained ground through strong primary performances, rising New Hampshire polling support near 22 percent in recent surveys, and consistent refusal to rule out a bid while prioritizing midterms. Midterm outcomes, early-state testing, and formal announcements after November 2026 could quickly consolidate support or open lanes for challengers.
